entities.summary: New Zealand is a sovereign nation in Australia and New Zealand, Oceania. Its capital is Wellington. Official languages include English, Māori (te reo Māori), New Zealand Sign Language. Government: Unitary parliamentary constitutional monarchy. Population: approximately 5.2 million. Area: 268,021 km². Comprehensive index for New Zealand / Aotearoa covering Polynesian voyaging and Māori settlement (~1250-1300 CE, one of last major landmasses settled by humans), Māori chiefdoms and intergroup warfare, Abel Tasman first European contact 1642, Cook voyages 1769-70, Treaty of Waitangi 1840 (founding document, British sovereignty, Māori rights, ongoing reinterpretation), New Zealand Wars 1845-72, land confiscation, gold rush, Dominion status 1907, ANZAC (Gallipoli 1915, national myth), women's suffrage 1893 (first in world), welfare state, WWII, anti-nuclear policy 1984 (ANZUS split), neoliberal reforms 1984 (Rogernomics), Treaty settlement process, Christchurch earthquake 2011, Christchurch mosque massacre 2019, COVID elimination strategy.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Treaty of Waitangi (1840) established British sovereignty over New Zealand while recognizing Māori rights, shaping the nation's identity and informing its ongoing struggle for self-determination. This founding document has been subject to reinterpretation and continues to influence New Zealand's politics and society.
